item.text: I’m reading the current three-file layout first, then I’ll pick the next refactor based on what responsibility is still awkwardly placed rather than just renaming more methods.

I found the next real design problem: `DirectedGraph` still depends on the demo facade just to answer `hasCycle()`. I’m removing that circular dependency by making the detector the algorithm entry point and having both callers route there directly.
That dependency cleanup is in place. I’m compiling and running the program now to confirm the new algorithm entry path behaves exactly the same.

I refactored the algorithm entry point so the graph model no longer depends on the demo facade.

`CycleDetector` now exposes the static algorithm entry `hasCycle(DirectedGraph)`, its constructor is private, and the internal run method was renamed to `containsCycle()` to make the instance lifecycle clearer. Both [DetectCycleDirectedGraph.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/029_detect_cycle_directed_graph/DetectCycleDirectedGraph.java) and [DirectedGraph.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/029_detect_cycle_directed_graph/DirectedGraph.java) now call into [CycleDetector.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/029_detect_cycle_directed_graph/CycleDetector.java) directly, which removes the previous circular dependency through `DetectCycleDirectedGraph`.
